results.summary: This Wokwi project takes an 8-bit binary value on its input pins and drives a 7-segment display to show the corresponding number. It is used by applying a binary pattern to the inputs and observing the display. The design requires an external 7-segment display connected to the outputs. It is a simple educational example of binary-to-display decoding.

This Wokwi project implements a half adder, a combinational circuit that adds two input bits to produce a sum and carry output. It is tested by setting the two inputs to all four combinations and checking the sum and carry outputs. No external hardware is required. The documentation is minimal and contains some grammatical errors, but the function is clear.

This Wokwi project implements a full adder, a combinational circuit that adds three input bits (A, B, and carry-in) to produce a sum and carry-out. It is tested by applying input combinations and verifying the outputs against a truth table. Regular LEDs are suggested as external hardware for visual output. The documentation is brief but sufficient to understand the design.

This Wokwi project implements a simple NAND gate with two inputs and one output. It is tested by applying input combinations according to a NAND truth table and monitoring the output. No external hardware is needed. The documentation is very brief but describes the basic function.

This Wokwi project reads two input pins and displays the corresponding decimal value on a display, with the display turning off when both inputs are set. It is tested by setting the inputs individually and together and observing the display. The external hardware required is a display, likely a 7-segment display, though not explicitly stated. The documentation is minimal and the project appears to be a first sample.

This Wokwi project is titled 'Hello World' and has a one-line description of 'Test'. The documentation states that the author does not know how it works or how to test it. The pins are labeled as generic inputs and outputs. There is essentially no documentation, so the design's function cannot be determined.

This Wokwi project blinks a 7-segment display at 1 Hz when the first DIP switch is turned on. It is tested by turning on the first DIP switch and observing the blinking. External hardware includes a DIP switch and a 7-segment display. The project is a simple test of segment blinking.

The documentation consists only of placeholder text, providing no information about the design's function or how to test it. The pins are labeled generically as ui0-ui7 and uo0-uo7. There is essentially no documentation, so the design's purpose cannot be determined.

This Wokwi project blinks an LED on a 7-segment display when switch 1 is set to on. It is tested by turning on switch 1, though the documentation notes there is nothing to test right now. No external hardware is required. The project is a simple LED blink test.
